title: Villeneuve, Toulon to Cádiz, 30 March to 9 April 1805 (the leg Stage A draws)
note: Table A of research/scene-02/h1-campaign.md, section 7, as checked in v-h1c.md (H1-35) and ruled in a-h1ac.md (H1-35e). The Atlas's noon latitudes are firm; her longitudes exist only for 1-3 and 10 April, so the other longitudes keep the line in the channels the sources name (est.). Refinements: start in the middle of the Grande Rade (the notes' 43°06'N 5°56'E falls in the inner road on the chart's coast); row 5 lies in the open sea south of the Gulf of Lion and row 6 SE (not SSE) of Barcelona; the Strait at about 11 a.m., not noon; the 4 p.m. point just past Cape Trafalgar, off Conil, at the adjudicated 36°14'N 6°11'W (the task text says 'off Cape Trafalgar rather than off Conil': a-h1ac's final statement puts it just past the cape, off Conil, the same water); an estimated point in the offing keeps the line about 3 nm off Cádiz's rocky west shore; the anchoring in open water about 3.2 nm west of Las Puercas and 2.5 nm west of the Los Cochinos buoy, outside the entrance shoals (Corbett: 'outside the bay'), not in the outer-bay berth of August-October. Dropped as adding nothing to the shape: the notes' estimated points east of Cabo de la Nao, off Garrucha and south of Málaga (the line keeps at least 3.5 nm off those coasts without them). Checked against Natural Earth 10m: the drawn curve keeps 2.2 nm or more from every cape (Cap Cépet 2.2, the coast east of Cartagena 2.5, Punta Cires about 2.5, Tarifa 4.1, Cape Trafalgar 4.9, Europa Point 6.4, Cape Spartel 10, Las Puercas 3.2, Cádiz west shore 2.8); only the leg out of Toulon road runs within 1 nm of the shore, as any exit from the road must.

title: Villeneuve, Cádiz to Martinique, 10 April to 14 May 1805
note: Table B: the Atlas's 32 dead-reckoning noon positions (Desbrière 1907, p. 26 n.), checked against the page image in v-h1c.md. Their dating is disputed (printed date or the day after; a-h1ac.md, H1-07), so no day marks: the dates below are the printed ones. Dropped: 8 May (16°00'N 46°23'W, 55 nm south of the line between 7 and 9 May) and 11 May (14°36'N 56°23'W, an impossible run of about 330 nm in a day). The last reckoning point lies about 1°50' east of the truth (36 leagues at the landfall); the line then runs to the landfall seven leagues east of Martinique, through the St Lucia Channel and up the lee coast past Diamond Rock (not in Natural Earth) to Fort-de-France. Main body 14 ships; four Spaniards crossed apart. All open-sea segments 2 nm or more from land.

title: Villeneuve, return to Europe, Cape Finisterre and Vigo, 10 June to 28 July 1805
note: Table D: Corbett's chart after Desbrière (±0.3°) with the Sally's noon position (British DR). Daily marks stop on 24 June; the line then runs straight to Corvo (2 July, Reille). Left out: the Curieux's 19 June position (the British report's 33°12'N 58°W lies two days ahead of the chart's marks; the chart's circle 30°13'N 58°06'W is on the line), James's 30 June point NE of Corvo (it would double back before Reille's 2 July sighting), the doubtful noon of 23 July (journal 43°41'N, 12°48' from Paris) and the '40 leagues WSW of Finisterre' of 27 July (a hairpin). The Z of 9-20 July is real, not reckoning noise: a NE gale on the 9th, the nearest approach west of Oporto on the 12th, then four days driven back west (Corbett 1910, p. 195); drop 12 and 16 July for a plain line. The action point is a-h1ac's smoke position. The entry to Vigo is by the south mouth of the ría (est.; the Cíes are not in Natural Earth); inside the ría the line runs 1-2 nm from the shore. Open-sea segments 2 nm or more from land (Corvo 13 nm, Cape Finisterre 38 nm).

title: Combined fleet, Ferrol to Cádiz, 13 to 20 August 1805
note: Table E: one British fix (the Iris, 14 August, Corbett 1910, p. 259 n.) and Reille's noon of the 15th (40 leagues WNW of Finisterre, about 43°39'N 11°48'W, 12 nm south of the line), the rest estimates. The 6 p.m.-2 a.m. stand towards Cape Prior on 13-14 August is left out (a hook). The turning point is an estimate (Reille's noon plus an afternoon's run). From 10 a.m. on 20 August the line runs straight into Cádiz bay, leaving out the morning's chase of Collingwood towards the Strait; it enters by the channel between Las Puercas and the El Diamante shoal (0.2-0.4 nm from the buoys, as the fairway is) to the berth in the outer bay of a-h2c.md, H2-36d. Open-sea segments 2 nm or more from land (Cape St Vincent 15-20 nm).

title: Nelson, Sardinia to Cape St Vincent, 3 April to 11 May 1805
note: Table F, corrected by a-h1b.md (Palmas 26-30 March, Pula 31 March-3 April, off Palermo 9-10 April not Ustica on the 7th, Lagos 9-11 May, the bear-away point SE of the cape). The line starts at Pula: the Palmas-Pula-Toro moves would double back along Sardinia's south coast. It loops to Palermo and back (two control points north of Capo San Vito keep the curve 8 nm or more off the cape; without them it crossed the cape). No positions were recorded on the beat west of 19-30 April (est.). Tetuan is entered and left as anchorages are; at Gibraltar the line touches the mouth of the bay (Nelson anchored there from 2 to 6 p.m. on 6 May), about 2 nm from Europa Point and Punta Carnero. Open-sea segments 2 nm or more from land.

title: Nelson, Cape St Vincent to Barbados, 11 May to 4 June 1805
note: Table G: the daily marks of Faden's chart of 1807 ('copied from his Lordship's original MS.') as Corbett redrew them, read at ±0.3°; the 14 May mark fits 'thirty-eight leagues from Madeira' (Nicolas VI 436). The last two points take the line round Barbados's south point into Carlisle Bay. All open-sea segments 3.6 nm or more from land (Madeira 26 nm).

waypoints.note: est., Barbados in sight at 6 a.m. on 4 June

title: Nelson in the West Indies, 5 to 12 June 1805
note: Table H: the places in the Victory's log and Nelson's letters (Nicolas VI 445-456); the passages between them estimated. The line goes in and out of the Gulf of Paria by the Boca Grande (a spur), passes south and west of Montserrat (the log's 'under Montserrat'; a straight line from Guadeloupe crossed the island) and approaches Antigua from the north-west, where the log puts the fleet at 6 a.m. on 12 June. Open-sea segments 2.3 nm or more from land (Redonda 3.5 nm); the anchorages at Carlisle Bay, the Gulf of Paria, St George's Bay and St John's Road are approached as harbours.

title: Nelson, Antigua to Gibraltar, 13 June to 19 July 1805
note: Table I: Faden's daily marks as Corbett redrew them (±0.3°), which agree with the log fixes of 29 June and 1 July within 0.3°. North of the Azores the 8 July log fix (São Miguel ESE by compass, 17½ leagues, computed with 21.1° W) replaces the chart's mark, and a-h1b's control point at 37°58'N 26°05'W keeps the line 3.3 nm off São Miguel's north coast (the route went through the islands, north of São Miguel). Dropped as zigzags: 24 June (31°43'N 52°56'W, a doubling back 70 nm west of the line) and 4 and 6 July (wobbles of 14-28 nm in the calms). The 13 July signal-log bearing does not fit and is not used. The last points take the line through the Strait, south of Punta Carnero, into Gibraltar Bay.

title: Nelson, Gibraltar to Ushant and Spithead, 22 July to 18 August 1805
note: Table J: estimates to Cape St Vincent, then Faden's marks as Corbett redrew them, with the diary's positions of 3 and 7 August (Desbrière 1907, pp. 74-75, read on the page images). Dropped as zigzags: 2, 4, 5 and 6 August (tacks against the northerlies, up to 30 nm either side of the line between the two diary positions). Left out: the Tetuan call of 22-25 July (a 25-nm spur). The Channel legs are estimates round St Catherine's Point and the east end of the Isle of Wight to Spithead. Open-sea segments 2 nm or more from land.
